\textbf{Written proof with same-agent verification; independent mathematical review and formalization pending.}

Retained-basis reconstruction, projected witnesses, and an additive maximum-branch charge improve the guarantee. The paper states the construction and source interfaces, proves the shared lemmas, and derives the selected coefficient below.

\section{Current theorem and dependencies}\label{current-theorem-and-dependencies}

For every known finite labeled matroid \(M\) on \(n\) elements, there is a measurable, distribution-independent online rule using one independent sample per label and \(42n+27\) initial independent fair bits. All sample/value coordinates are mutually independent and nonnegative, with matching laws at each label, and the seed is independent. Assume only that \(\mathbb E[\operatorname{OPT}_M(V)]<\infty\). For every measurable arrival permutation depending on all samples, all values, and the entire seed, the accepted set is independent after every prefix and

\[\mathbb E[\mathrm{reward}]\ge C_\star\mathbb E[\operatorname{OPT}_M(V)],\qquad
C_\star=\frac{548933908320757}{1325382348737372749824000}>\frac{7}{4}\, 2^{-32}.\]

The exact certificate is approximately \textbf{1.71459 times} the preceding \href{https://github.com/shea256/matroid-prophet-inequality/blob/master/results/rank-charged.md}{\texttt{2\^{}-32} certificate} (\textbf{71.46\% higher}). This compares guaranteed fractions, not measured performance.

We retain the density paths, generators, hybrid safety comparison, marked-pivot machinery, rank accounting, and lossless simulation from \href{https://github.com/openai/math/blob/fd4aeeb2ee4fc729c18d98444fed42fd0529eeeb/preprints/One-Sample-Suffices-for-Matroid-Prophet-Inequalities-against-an-Almighty-Adversary-September-23-2026/final.pdf}{OpenAI's pinned manuscript}. Their interfaces are specified below. Computation and storage may be exponential, with exact observations; no polynomial-time claim is made.

\section{The fixed-vector rule and its statistics}\label{the-fixed-vector-rule-and-its-statistics}

Fix a nonnegative hidden vector \(w\) before any seed bits. The rule reveals and sacrifices a seed-chosen mask and must handle every permutation; its target is \(\mathbb{E}_R\min_\pi w(A(w,R,\pi))\) . Write \(\operatorname{r}(A\mid P)=\operatorname{r}(A\cup P)-\operatorname{r}(P)\) and \(F_{\varnothing}=\operatorname{cl}(\varnothing)\) . Fix a label order for every tie. Higher rounded weight means higher priority. Put \(W=\operatorname{OPT}_M(u)\) and let \(I^*\) be priority greedy on the full rounded vector.

Let \(\kappa\ge4\) , \(0<h,\rho,t<1\) , integer \(L\ge1\) , and \(\theta>1\) be fixed parameters supplied by the selected result. The independent masks \(H,D,C,T\) have rates \(h,\rho,t,t\) respectively. The main branch has probability \(1-t\) ; parity is fair. Choose a uniform shared phase \(J\in\{0,\ldots,L-1\}\) , set \(B=\theta^L\) , and define

\[u_J(x)=\theta^J B^{\lfloor\log_B(x/\theta^J)\rfloor}\quad(x>0),\qquad u_J(0)=0.\]

All random choices are made initially. Each result supplies exact dyadic mask probabilities and a finite fair-bit implementation. The score variables in the counting proof below are analysis devices, not algorithmic inputs.

The maximum branch reveals a separate fair mask and accepts the first unmasked positive nonloop with priority above every revealed positive nonloop. An empty threshold is below every positive nonloop. If \(m_*\) is the largest rounded nonloop weight, expected worst-order reward is at least \(m_*/4\) : the largest-priority nonloop is unmasked and the second is masked with probability \(1/4\) . With only one positive nonloop success has probability \(1/2\) ; with none the bound is zero.

In the main branch reveal and sacrifice \(H\cup D\cup C\) . Define

\[U=\{e\notin H:u_e>0,\ e\notin\operatorname{cl}(H_{>e})\},\qquad Y=I^*\setminus H.\]

The candidate test uses only revealed \(H\) values and the tested value. For a fixed phase divide weights by \(\theta^J\) , so true groups \(U_i\) have weight \(B^i\) . List those meeting \(D\) in increasing weight order as \(G_1,\ldots,G_m\) ; put \(D_j=D\cap G_j\) , and similarly \(C_j,T_j\) . The full groups are analysis objects; their revealed \(D_j,C_j\) parts suffice for preparation. If there are no listed groups, reject all.

For a flat \(P\) , let \(Q_j(P)\) be the largest flat \(Z\supseteq P\) maximizing \(|D_j\cap Z|-\kappa\operatorname{r}(Z)\) . Take closure first for nonflat arguments. Set \(a_j=-3j\) and enable \(Q_{j,k}=Q_j\) for \(k\ge a_j\) , with the identity earlier. Starting from \(F_0(k)=F_{\varnothing}\) for \(k<0\) and \(E\) otherwise, define

\[X_j(k)=Q_{j,k}(F_{j-1}(k)),\qquad
 F_j(k)=\operatorname{cl}(X_j(k)\cup(C_j\cap X_j(k+1))).\]

Compute paths in increasing \(j\) on the finite relevant auxiliary timeline, and put \(\widehat F=F_m\) . For a candidate nonloop in listed group \(j\) , write \(b_j(e)=\min\{k:e\in X_j(k)\}\) . It is eligible precisely when it is unsacrificed, \(T\) -positive, has birth \(b\ge a_j+2\) of the chosen parity, and lies outside \(\widehat F(b-2)\) . At endpoint \(b\) maintain a set \(A_b\) ; accept an eligible \(e\) exactly when \(\operatorname{r}(\{e\}\mid\widehat F(b-2)\cup A_b)=1\) .

The source density and path lemmas give

\[F_{j-1}(k)\subseteq X_j(k)\subseteq F_j(k)\subseteq X_j(k+1),\qquad
 |D_j\cap(\operatorname{cl}(Q_j(P)\cup Z)\setminus Q_j(P))|\le\kappa\operatorname{r}(Z\mid Q_j(P)).\]

Nonloops are born at \(a_j\) or in \([a_j+2,0]\) , and the entire nominal path uses a generator set of size at most \(|D_j|/\kappa\) . The nested layer bases give prefix independence. Finite rank operations, fixed tie rules, and countably many rounding levels give measurability. These structural facts are inherited from the cited source.

For valid selected-parity endpoints \(a_j+2\le b\le0\) , define

\[\begin{aligned}
 K_{j,b}&=\bigcup_{\ell<j}(T_\ell\cap(X_\ell(b)\setminus X_\ell(b-1))),\\
 P_{j,b}&=G_j\cap(X_j(b)\setminus X_j(b-1)),\quad
 O=D\cup C,\quad S_{j,b}=P_{j,b}\setminus O,\\
 z_j&=\sum_b\operatorname{r}(S_{j,b}\mid X_j(b-2)\cup K_{j,b}),\\
 \lambda_j&=\sum_b\operatorname{r}(T_j\cap S_{j,b}\mid\widehat F(b-2)\cup K_{j,b}).
 \end{aligned}\]

The safe count \(\sigma_j\) counts \(d\in D_j\cap Y\) with such a birth and \(d\notin Q_j(F_{j-1}(b-2)\cup K_{j,b})\) . For each nominal summand choose a fixed-order basis extension \(Z_b\) , so \(\sum_b|Z_b|=z_j\) . The residual is

\[\mathcal R_j=\bigcup_b\left(P_{j,b}\setminus
 \operatorname{cl}(X_j(b-2)\cup K_{j,b}\cup Z_b)\right)\subseteq O.\]

Extend \(\sigma_i,z_i,\lambda_i\) by zero on unlisted true groups. The source density argument gives \(\sigma_j\le\kappa z_j+|\mathcal R_j|\) . Its order-uniform lemma bounds the number of accepts of weight at least that of \(G_j\) below by \(\lambda_j\) , for every seed and order. One later-path generator budget over the whole timeline is

\[c_j=|C_j|+\sum_{\ell>j}(|C_\ell|+|D_\ell|/\kappa).\]

Conditional on \(H,D,C\) , parity, and test bits outside the focal group, independent test thinning gives \(\mathbb{E}[\lambda_j\mid\mathcal F_{-j}] \ge t(z_j-c_j)\) . These are the source interfaces used below.

\section{A quadratic transaction inequality}\label{a-quadratic-transaction-inequality}

\textbf{Quadratic transaction lemma.} Let \(\mathcal A\) be an increasing event on finitely many independent bits, and let a predictable query procedure, reading each bit at most once, determine whether \(\mathcal A\) occurs. Write \(p=\mathbb{P}(\mathcal A^c)\) . At the completed transcript let \(q\) be the failure probability with only unqueried bits random and every queried bit reset to zero. Then

\[\mathbb{E}[\mathbf 1_{\mathcal A}q^2]\ge p(1-p).\]

\textbf{Proof.} At an intermediate transcript, let \(W\) be its remaining coordinates and \(I\) its queried positives. Let \(m\) be the actual conditional failure probability, and \(q\) the failure probability with only \(W\) random and all other bits zero. Predictable product exposure identifies \(m\) with the probability when \(I\) is forced positive and \(W\) is random. Increasingness gives \(0\le m\le q\le1\) . Initially \(m=q=p\) .

For a predictably chosen next coordinate, the depleted probability \(q'\) is determined before the answer and satisfies \(q'\ge q\) . The actual conditional failure probability is a martingale: \(\mathbb{E}[m'\mid\text{transcript}]=m\) . Therefore the potential \(\Phi(q,m)=q^2-2qm\) satisfies

\[\mathbb{E}[\Phi(q',m')\mid\text{transcript}]-\Phi(q,m)
 =(q'-q)(q'+q-2m)\ge0.\]

At the end \(m=\mathbf 1_{\mathcal A^c}\) , and failure forces \(q=1\) . The initial potential is \(-p^2\) ; its final expectation is \(\mathbb{E}[\mathbf 1_{\mathcal A}q^2]-p\) . Sum the displayed query identity over the finite number of queries, padding stopped paths by zeros, to obtain the result. The proof includes \(p=0,1\) and transactions needing no queries.

\section{The reverse exit hazard}\label{the-reverse-exit-hazard}

Fix the source's filter and density masks, a listed-group prefix, and a nonloop \(d\) still alive before a reverse step. Its current states are \(S\) , and its transition is \(\mathcal G_k(c,S)\) . The remaining guard coordinates have their product law. Let \(\mathcal A\) be the increasing event that \(d\) survives, and let \(p\) be the conditional exit probability.

For completeness, for \(k<0\) the source reverse map on a listed-group prefix is defined recursively by

\[A_0=F_{\varnothing},\qquad N_j=Q_{j,k}(A_{j-1}),\qquad
 A_j=\operatorname{cl}(N_j\cup\{e\in G_j\cap S_j:c_e=1\}),\]

with output \((N_j)_j\) . Starting from \(X_j(0)=E\) , reverse steps compute \(X(k)=\mathcal G_k(C,X(k+1))\) . For actual later states, \(N_j\subseteq S_j\) for every fresh bit assignment. After computing \(N_j\) , query only \(G_j\cap(S_j\setminus N_j)\) ; omitted additions already lie in \(N_j\) . The new remaining domain is \(\bigcup_j(G_j\cap N_j)\) .

The source queries exactly the departing coordinates in predictable batches. Their answers determine all output states: unqueried bits are inside flats already spanned. Thus the transcript decides \(\mathcal A\) , on both survival and failure, so the quadratic transaction lemma applies.

Let \(S'\) be the actual output and \(V'\) the remaining coordinates. For each assignment \(c\) supported on \(V'\) , monotonicity in time and state gives

\[\mathcal G_{k-1}(c,S')\subseteq\mathcal G_k(c,S).\]

The right side has all just-queried coordinates zero, exactly the depleted experiment defining \(q\) . Conditional on the full post-step transcript, the bits in \(V'\) remain independent. On survival the next hazard \(r\) therefore satisfies \(r\ge q\) . The states are frozen in this comparison; earlier states are not recomputed after resetting bits. No order is conditioned on.

The next alive squared hazard consequently obeys

\[\mathbb{E}[\mathbf 1_{\rm survive}r^2]-p^2\ge p-2p^2.\]

Telescope this potential over the deterministic finite reverse horizon. Every nonloop exits, and if \(P\) is its hazard at actual exit, then

\[-p_{\rm start}^2\ge
 \sum_i\mathbb{E}[\mathbf 1_{\rm alive}p_i]-2\sum_i\mathbb{E}[\mathbf 1_{\rm alive}p_i^2]
 =1-2\mathbb{E}P.\]

Hence

\[\boxed{\mathbb{E}P\ge(1+p_{\rm start}^2)/2\ge1/2.}\]

In particular, the source's total squared-exit mass is at least \(1/2\) . Its hybrid comparison still applies because guard and test rates agree. The same baseline-birth loss and fair parity give, after averaging a density mask of arbitrary rate \(\rho\) ,

\[\mathbb{E}[\sigma_i\mid H]\ge \gamma|Y_i|-\frac{\rho n_i}{2\kappa},
 \qquad\gamma=\rho/4.\]

This averages before conditioning on listing, extending the statistics by zero on unlisted groups.

The bound \(1/2\) is sharp for the abstract hypotheses. Take \(N\) Bernoulli-\(t\) bits and repeatedly test the OR of the remaining suffix, querying until the first positive or until that suffix is exhausted. The next hazard equals the depleted current failure probability. With \(a=1-t\) , classification by the last positive (or none) gives

\[\mathbb{E}P=a^{2N}+t\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}a^{2j}
 =a^{2N}+\frac{1-a^{2N}}{2-t}.\]

For \(t=1/m\) , \(N=m^2\) , this tends to \(1/2\) . This is an abstract limitation, not a hard matroid instance or a bound on the best prophet algorithm.

\section{Joint residual encoding}\label{joint-residual-encoding}

Fix \(H\) , parity, and all mask bits outside a true group \(U\) of size \(n\ge\kappa\) . Do not condition on its focal bits or listing. Its incoming path \(F(k)\) , competition sets \(K_b\) , index, and activation \(a\) are fixed. Write \(S_d(N)=\sum_{i=0}^d\binom Ni\) . Suppose a path has density generators \(J\) and rank witnesses \(Z\) , of sizes \(j,z\) . A generator has insertion time \(\tau(g)\in[a,0]\) , and

\[X(k)=\operatorname{cl}(F(k)\cup\{g\in J:\tau(g)\le k\}).\]

The source gives two marked streams. First, list \(F(k)\) and then generators inserted at \(k\) , marking the block one exactly when \(k\) is a valid endpoint of the chosen parity. Second, start with the fixed \(F(b_0)\) marked zero, where \(b_0\in\{a-2,a-1\}\) has that parity. At each subsequent parity endpoint \(b\) , insert \(K_b,Z_b\) with mark zero, then \(F(b)\) and generators with \(b-2<\tau(g)\le b\) with mark one. End at \(b_1\in\{0,1\}\) of that parity; set \(K_b=Z_b=\varnothing\) at invalid endpoints.

The second stream has intermediate span \(\operatorname{cl}(X(b-2)\cup K_b\cup Z_b)\) and endpoint span \(X(b)\) , since \(K_b\subseteq F(b)\) and \(Z_b\subseteq X(b)\) . The first test selects valid births. For a label passing it, the second pivot lies in the same layer and has mark one exactly on the residual. Thus the intersection of the two mark-one sets is the residual.

\textbf{Joint pivot lemma.} For fixed \(J,Z\) , the number of residuals obtained from these linked streams is at most \(3^j4^{2j+z}S_{j+z}(2n)\) .

\textbf{Proof.} The source marked-pivot argument first bounds retained greedy bases of occurrences by \(4^s\) when \(s\) specified movable occurrences are inserted into an old sequence spanning the matroid. To recall why, old-only greedy gives an ordered basis. Only at most \(s\) of its positions can be omitted after insertions: their conditional-rank drops for the full movable set sum to at most \(s\) . There are at most \(2^s\) choices of omitted old occurrences and \(2^s\) of retained movable occurrences. Apply this to the two streams with \(s=j\) and \(s=j+z\) , giving \(4^{2j+z}\) pairs of retained bases. Fix a pair. Each nonloop has a unique minimal support in each basis, by matroid submodularity, and its pivot is the last support member.

We represent both streams by the same \(j+z\) variables. Label the entire ground set \(0,\ldots,N-1\) , put \(m=N+1\) , \(T=8m\) , and \(u_k=(k-a+2)T\) . Give old \(F(k)\) occurrences in the first stream absolute scores \(2^{u_k+4m+e}\) , with sign equal to their fixed marks. In the second stream, the initial \(F(b_0)\) has negative scores \(-2^{u_{b_0}+4m+e}\) ; \(K_b\) has scores \(-2^{u_b+e}\) ; and \(F(b)\) has scores \(2^{u_b+4m+e}\) . These are fixed before the focal masks.

Give each generator a variable \(x_g=2^{u_{\tau(g)}+6m+g}\) . Its first score is \(\eta_gx_g\) , positive exactly at a valid endpoint. Its second score is \(d_gx_g\) , where \(d_g=1\) for the chosen parity and \(d_g=2^T\) otherwise. Multiplication by \(2^T\) moves an insertion from \(b-1\) into the endpoint \(b\) block. Give each witness \(e\in Z_b\) a variable \(y_e=2^{u_b+2m+e}\) , used only as the score \(-y_e\) in the second stream. There are only three types for a generator:

\[(\eta_g,d_g)\in\{(1,1),(-1,1),(-1,2^T)\}.\]

The middle type includes early insertions of the chosen parity that are not valid births. Fix all types, at a cost of at most \(3^j\) choices. Order every block by label. Second-stream generators can be reordered within their endpoint block because all have mark one; this preserves pivot marks and endpoint spans, and all retained bases are already counted.

In each stream the absolute scores are distinct powers of two in occurrence order. Every score dominates the sum of its predecessors. The sign of the sum over a support therefore equals its last member's mark. For fixed bases and types these are \(2n\) affine functions of the same \(j+z\) variables. Every realized mark pair is a strict sign pattern. The hyperplane-region bound gives at most \(S_{j+z}(2n)\) patterns, proving the claim. Ground-set size and timeline length affect coefficients, not this dimension bound.

\section{From a rank estimate to the final guarantee}\label{from-a-rank-estimate-to-the-final-guarantee}

Earlier versions use \(a_0=0\) and \(\bar\gamma=\rho/4\). The current refinement keeps a fixed additive error and pays for it with the maximum branch.

The selected result must supply constants \(K>0\), \(\epsilon,a_0\ge0\), and \(0<\bar\gamma\le\rho/4\) such that, for each true group of size \(n_i\ge\kappa\) ,

\[\mathbb E[z_i\mid H]\ge\frac{\bar\gamma|Y_i|-\epsilon n_i-a_0}{K}.\]

The source's later-path cost, including unlisted groups by domination, obeys

\[\mathbb E[c_i\mid H]\le t n_i+(t+\rho/\kappa)\sum_{j>i}n_j.\]

Independent focal test thinning therefore gives

\[\mathbb E[\lambda_i\mid H]\ge\frac tK\left[
\bar\gamma|Y_i|-(\epsilon+Kt)n_i-
(Kt+K\rho/\kappa)\sum_{j>i}n_j-a_0\right].\]

Both changed cost factors are essential when \(K\ne\kappa\) . For general filter rate \(h\) , the source filter argument gives

\[\mathbb E_H u(Y)=(1-h)W,\qquad
\mathbb E_H u(U)=\frac{1-h}{h}\mathbb E_Hu(\operatorname{greedy}(H))
\le\frac{1-h}{h}W.\]

To verify the identity, condition on memberships preceding each label in rounded priority. Its span test is fixed. The candidate and sample-greedy probabilities are respectively \(1-h\) and \(h\) times this test; sum their weighted contributions. The comparison set \(Y\) remains independent and contained in \(U\) .

Set \(\beta=(B-1)/B\) and

\[L_0=\epsilon+Kt+\frac{Kt+K\rho/\kappa}{B-1},\qquad
s=(1-h)(\bar\gamma-L_0/h).\]

For every fixed seed and arrival permutation, the source order-uniform rank bound implies that the number accepted at weight at least \(B^i\) is at least \(\lambda_i\) . An accepted weight \(B^\ell\) contributes at most \(\sum_{i\le\ell}B^i=B^\ell/\beta\) to this cumulative sum. Consequently

\[\min_\pi u(A_{\mathrm{main}}(R,\pi))
\ge\beta\sum_{i:n_i\ge\kappa}B^i\lambda_i.\]

The weighted higher-group cost is at most \(u(U)/(B-1)\) . Discarding groups smaller than \(\kappa\) loses comparison mass at most \(\kappa m_*/\beta\) , where \(m_*\) is the largest rounded nonloop weight. The geometric sum of the weights of analyzed groups is at most \(m_*/\beta\), so their additive errors contribute at most \(t a_0m_*/K\). Applying the filter identities yields

\[\mathbb E_R\min_\pi\mathrm{reward}_{\mathrm{main}}
\ge\frac{\beta t s}{K}W-\frac{t(\bar\gamma\kappa+a_0)}{K}m_*.\]

If \((1-t)t(\bar\gamma\kappa+a_0)/K\le t/4\) , the maximum branch cancels the negative term. This condition is checked by the selected result's exact certificate. For positive \(x\) , let \(k=\lfloor\log_\theta x\rfloor\) . Across the \(L\) phases its rounded values are \(\theta^{k-r}\) , once each for \(r=0,\ldots,L-1\) . Since \(\theta^k\ge x/\theta\) , the geometric sum gives

\[\mathbb E_Ju_J(x)\ge\frac{\beta}{L(\theta-1)}x.\]

Apply this to one fixed true optimal independent set to obtain the same factor for the rounded optimum. Thus, provided \(s>0\) , the coefficient is

\[C=\frac{(1-t)\beta^2 t s}{L(\theta-1)K}.\]

The minimum over permutations remains inside the seed expectation at every stage, including phase and branch. The source's glued-vector simulation reveals and sacrifices the mask fixed by the seed, using the sample there and the online value elsewhere. Conditional on the entire seed this glued vector has the original product value law, so it is independent of the seed. Ignored samples, sacrificed values, and unused coins may still inform the adversary's chosen permutation; the pointwise minimum covers them all.

\section{Resources and proof dependencies}\label{resources-and-proof-dependencies}

The rule uses a known finite labeled matroid, independent nonnegative values and matching independent samples, and exact observations. Only the expected offline optimum needs to be finite. Rank/closure tables and flat enumeration may be exponential; preprocessing and storage are part of the construction. There are finitely many occupied groups and a finite relevant auxiliary timeline. Observation precision and integer level indices are unbounded in the original measurable model. For rational inputs, exact power comparisons have costs depending on bit lengths and exponents. No polynomial complexity or practical performance claim is made.

The source density, generator, path, feasibility, hybrid safety, thinning, order-uniform rank, and simulation lemmas remain explicit dependencies. The quadratic and joint pivot proofs above are this project's written refinements. Exact certificates prove their scalar assertions, and finite checks test their specified cases. Independent mathematical review and formalization of these refinements remain pending.

\section{Retained bases and projected residuals}\label{retained-bases-and-projected-residuals}

The \href{https://github.com/shea256/matroid-prophet-inequality/blob/master/paper/framework.md}{shared framework} supplies the construction, quadratic safety estimate, two marked streams, joint affine representation, and order-uniform accounting. We improve the residual count, retain its fixed tail error as an additive term, and restrict the witnesses and tested labels to the comparison optimum. Only the algorithm's parameters change; the comparison optimum remains an analysis object.

\subsection{Retained insertions determine the old basis}\label{retained-insertions-determine-the-old-basis}

\textbf{Reconstruction lemma.} Fix an ordered list of old occurrences in a finite matroid and interleave specified movable occurrences arbitrarily. If the greedy scan retains movable occurrence set \(T\), its retained old occurrences are exactly the greedy scan of the old list after contracting the labels of \(T\). Thus \(s\) specified movable occurrences admit at most \(2^s\) retained bases of occurrences.

\textbf{Proof.} Let \(A\) be the retained old occurrences preceding an old occurrence \(e\). If the interleaved scan rejects \(e\), its label is spanned by \(A\) and the movable occurrences already retained, a subset of \(T\). It is therefore spanned by \(A\cup T\). If the scan retains \(e\), the final retained set is independent and contains \(A\cup T\cup\{e\}\), so \(e\) increases rank over \(A\cup T\). Induction over the old list proves the contraction-scan identity. Occurrences are distinguished even when labels repeat; retained occurrences cannot repeat a label or be loops. The argument includes \(T=\varnothing\). For fixed \(T\) the whole retained basis is fixed, and there are at most \(2^s\) choices of \(T\).

In particular, the source's general marked-pivot bound improves from \(4^sS_s(m)\) to \(2^sS_s(m)\) with its affine-sign proof unchanged. For the actual two streams, forced retention gives a stronger bound still.

Choose the density generators by the source's canonical forward extension rule. At time \(k\), the first-stream prefix before the new generators spans \(\operatorname{cl}(F(k)\cup X(k-1))\). Each new generator increases rank over this flat and earlier generators in its batch. Every generator is therefore retained in that stream, so its retained basis has one possibility for fixed generator set \(J\).

Every witness in \(Z_b\) is retained in the second stream: its prefix spans \(X(b-2)\cup K_b\), and \(Z_b\) is an independent extension over that base. The same-mark generator reorderings in the joint affine representation leave endpoint spans unchanged, so this remains true after reordering. For fixed \(J,Z\), the second retained movable set is \(Z\cup J'\) for some \(J'\subseteq J\). The reconstruction lemma gives at most \(2^j\) second bases, where \(j=|J|\), with no factor depending on \(z=|Z|\). Second-stream generators are not all forced; the finite checks include omitted ones.

Keep the three generator types and the same \(j+z\) variables from the joint affine representation. On any fixed set of \(m\) tested labels, its \(2m\) affine forms have at most \(S_{j+z}(2m)\) strict sign patterns. Consequently, for fixed \(J,Z\), the residual count is at most

\[6^jS_{j+z}(2m).\]

This counts the restricted streams having the forced-retention properties; every actual stream belongs to this family. Old paths, retained bases for each subset, and affine coefficients are fixed before the focal masks. Timeline length affects coefficients, not dimension. All three generator types, including early invalid insertions, remain charged.

\subsection{Project the witnesses and residual onto the comparison optimum}\label{project-the-witnesses-and-residual-onto-the-comparison-optimum}

Fix a phase and filter \(H\), and let \(I^*\) be the fixed tie-broken optimum of the rounded full vector. Put \(Y=I^*\setminus H\). For a true group \(U\), write \(n=|U|\) and \(y=|Y\cap U|\). Condition further on parity and masks outside \(U\), without conditioning on listing or any focal bits. Both \(U\) and \(Y\cap U\) are fixed. The online rule does not receive or compute \(I^*\).

At each valid nominal birth layer choose, by fixed label order, a basis extension

\[Z_b'\subseteq(P_b\cap Y)\setminus O
\quad\text{over }X(b-2)\cup K_b,\qquad O=D\cup C.\]

Let \(z'=\sum_b|Z_b'|\) and

\[R_Y=\bigcup_b\left[(P_b\cap Y)\setminus
\operatorname{cl}(X(b-2)\cup K_b\cup Z_b')\right].\]

The layers are disjoint, so \(Z'=\bigcup_bZ_b'\) has size \(z'\) and is contained in \(Y\cap U\). Its spanning property gives \(R_Y\subseteq O\). All safe samples counted in \(\sigma\) lie in \(Y\). A safe sample at layer \(b\) outside \(R_Y\) lies in the witness span but outside \(Q'_b=Q(F(b-2)\cup K_b)\). Since \(X(b-2)\cup K_b\subseteq Q'_b\), the source density inequality bounds their number by \(\kappa\operatorname{r}(Z_b'\mid Q'_b)\le\kappa|Z_b'|\). Thus

\[\sigma\le\kappa z'+|R_Y|.\]

The full nominal statistic satisfies \(z\ge z'\) by rank monotonicity in each layer. Lower-bounding \(z'\) therefore lower-bounds the full \(z\) in the original test-thinning lemma. The alternative witnesses use no focal test bits.

Use \(Z_b'\) in the two streams and test only \(Y\cap U\). Their mark-one intersection is exactly \(R_Y\), and both forced-retention properties continue to hold. Summing over generator and witness subsets gives fixed families

\[|\mathcal F_{j,z'}|\le
\binom nj\binom y{z'}6^jS_{j+z'}(2y).\]

Impossible subset choices only overcount. Generators may overlap the tested labels; no independence involving their adaptive selection is used. This bound includes zero sizes and dimensions exceeding \(2y\).

\subsection{Weighted entropy and the additive error}\label{weighted-entropy-and-the-additive-error}

Put \(p=\rho+(1-\rho)t\), \(\lambda=-\log p\), and choose penalties \(\mu,\nu>0\) and tilts \(0<u,w,v<1\) with

\[6e^{-\lambda\mu}/v\le u,\qquad e^{-\lambda\nu}/v\le w.\]

For every integer \(d\ge0\), \(v^dS_d(2y)\le(1+v)^{2y}\), because \(v^d\le v^i\) for \(i\le d\) and the binomial expansion bounds the sum. The binomial theorem therefore gives

\[\begin{aligned}
\sum_{j=0}^n\sum_{z'=0}^y|\mathcal F_{j,z'}|
 e^{-\lambda(\mu j+\nu z')}
&\le(1+u)^n(1+w)^y(1+v)^{2y}\\
&\le\exp\bigl(n\,u+y(w+2v)\bigr).
\end{aligned}\]

On listed outcomes set \(e=(|R_Y|-\mu j-\nu z')_+\) and set \(e=0\) otherwise. Each fixed family member has containment probability \(\Pr(R\subseteq O)=p^{|R|}\) under the original product law. Taking a union over all fixed families handles the mask-dependent selection and gives

\[\Pr(e>x)\le\min\{1,\exp(n\,u+y(w+2v)-\lambda x)\},\qquad
\mathbb E e\le\frac{n\,u+y(w+2v)+1}{\lambda}.\]

The integral splits at \([n\,u+y(w+2v)]/\lambda\). We keep its constant \(1/\lambda\) additive. No probability for \(J\subseteq D\) is multiplied into the containment bound, since those sets could overlap.

The projected residual comparison and generator budget imply pointwise

\[\sigma\le(\kappa+\nu)z'+\frac\mu\kappa|D\cap U|+e.\]

On unlisted outcomes \(\sigma=z'=e=0\), so this inequality still holds. Average the tail bound and then use the quadratic safety estimate, averaged over parity. For any \(0<d\le\lambda\), the framework's rank interface holds with

\[K=\kappa+\nu,\qquad
\bar\gamma=\rho/4-(w+2v)/d,\qquad
\epsilon=\frac\rho{2\kappa}+\frac{\mu\rho}{\kappa}+u/d,
\qquad a_0=1/d.\]

We require \(\bar\gamma>0\). The tail bound holds for each parity and outside mask; the safety estimate is used only after averaging those conditions. The framework carries both changed cost factors, \(Kt\) and \(K\rho/\kappa\), and charges the additive term through the geometric weight sum. Its maximum branch cancels the combined loss precisely when

\[(1-t)(\bar\gamma\kappa+a_0)/K\le1/4.\]

This additional condition is essential. Dropping the constant without charging it would be invalid. The order minimum remains inside all seed expectations, including branch and phase, and the original lossless one-sample simulation still applies.

\subsection{Parameters and final coefficient}\label{parameters-and-final-coefficient}

Choose the algorithmic parameters

\[\kappa=192,\quad\rho=3/8,\quad h=3/4,\quad t=21/2^{18},\qquad
\theta=261/256,\quad L=256,\quad p_{\rm main}=1-t,\]

and analysis constants

\[\begin{gathered}
\mu=119/8,\quad\nu=243/16,\quad K=3315/16,\\
u=1/512,\quad w=1/4096,\quad v=1/704,\quad d=49/50.
\end{gathered}\]

The \href{https://github.com/shea256/matroid-prophet-inequality/blob/master/verification/certify_retained_basis.py}{exact certificate} verifies \(\lambda>d\), both tilt inequalities, and \(B>140\) using outward rational log intervals. Separate exact power comparisons,

\[6^8p^{119}<(uv)^8,\qquad p^{243}<(wv)^{16},\]

verify the same tilts. A separate 20-term positive atanh sum checks the decay lower bound without range reduction. Using the rounded \(49/50\) alone for the first tilt would fail; it is used only in the error accounting.

Direct substitution gives

\[\bar\gamma=\frac{100013}{1103872},\qquad
\epsilon=\frac{6427}{200704},\qquad a_0=\frac{50}{49},\qquad
s>\frac{1280616385}{235681087488}>0.\]

Use \(\beta>139/140\), \(B-1>139\), and \(L(\theta-1)=5\) in the framework's final coefficient. The maximum-branch condition holds, and the coefficient exceeds

\[C_3=\frac{548933908320757}{1325382348737372749824000}
>\frac74\,2^{-32}.\]

This is approximately \(4.14170227062\times10^{-10}\), or \(1.71459364062\) times the preceding exact \(C_2\): a \(71.46\%\) increase in the guaranteed fraction. It remains below \(2^{-31}\). It is approximately \(27.35368\) times the earlier announced \(C_0\) certificate above \(2^{-36}\). These compare guarantees, not measured performance. The certificate separately reconstructs \(C_2\) before comparing it.

All probabilities are dyadic. The seed uses \(2+3+18+18+1=42\) fair bits per label and \(8+18+1=27\) shared bits, compared with the previous \(36n+23\) total. Every bit is drawn initially, including unused-branch randomness. The new witnesses, tilts, and penalties are analysis devices; they require no access to the optimum, additional samples, or algorithmic work. The shared exact-real and potentially exponential preprocessing/storage model is unchanged.

\subsection{Verification and review}\label{verification-and-review}

The \href{https://github.com/shea256/matroid-prophet-inequality/blob/master/experiments/search_retained_basis.py}{numerical search} uses 16 deterministic starts per cumulative mode. Its best floating multiple of \(2^{-32}\) was about \(1.78594\); the certified coefficient is about \(1.77885\). No global optimum or ceiling is established.

The \href{https://github.com/shea256/matroid-prophet-inequality/blob/master/verification/check_retained_basis.py}{finite checker} tests 74,881 interleavings over all 92 labeled matroids through four elements, with up to two movable occurrences and forward/reverse old orders. It checks 3,349 basis-family bounds and 45,824 projected encodings/charges on 170 small matroid-weight instances. Actual paths use threshold 2, an empty filter mask, and stress penalties, with omitted second generators, strict rank/projection savings, adaptive containment tails, and an additive-error negative control. These checks do not prove the universal statements for arbitrary matroids.

The \href{https://github.com/shea256/matroid-prophet-inequality/blob/master/proofs/retained_basis_audit.md}{same-agent audit} records the proof obligations. Independent mathematical review and formalization remain pending. The source refresh and comparison limits are recorded in \href{https://github.com/shea256/matroid-prophet-inequality/blob/master/BASELINE.md}{BASELINE}.

\section{Sources, attribution, and comparison limits}\label{sources-attribution-and-comparison-limits}

OpenAI supplies the original qualitative constant guarantee and construction in \emph{One Sample Suffices for Matroid Prophet Inequalities against an Almighty Adversary}, September 23, 2026, pinned at \href{https://github.com/openai/math/tree/fd4aeeb2ee4fc729c18d98444fed42fd0529eeeb}{revision fd4aeeb2ee4f}. Its density paths, reverse exposure, hybrid comparison, marked-pivot machinery, rank accounting, and lossless sample/value simulation are fundamental inputs. The manuscript derives \(2^{-293}\), stronger than its \(2^{-310}\) headline. The secretary consequence is in the same manuscript. Primary sources and hashes are recorded in \href{https://github.com/shea256/matroid-prophet-inequality/blob/master/BASELINE.md}{the baseline}.

This project's quadratic potential, joint affine encoding, and application of weighted residual counting refine that construction's quantitative analysis. The current version reconstructs old retained bases by contraction, uses forced retained occurrences, projects witnesses onto the comparison optimum, and pays the tail's additive constant through the maximum branch. Greedy scanning in a contracted matroid is standard; the claimed refinement is its application and the resulting quantitative accounting here. Exponential weighting, union bounds, finite-offset rounding, and binomial estimates are established methods; no new general principle is claimed for them. Each version retains its specific evidence and source credit in the result registry and archives.

Daniel (@firsttimelifer) \href{https://x.com/firsttimelifer/status/2108282829809541468}{announced} a \(2^{-47}\) guarantee on October 8, 2026. A supporting manuscript was not located in the October 10 audit; its assumptions and proof remain unverified. It is acknowledged as an announcement, not an established comparison baseline. The \(1/2\) prophet result in \href{https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19118v1}{Abdi, Banihashem, Hajiaghayi, and Mittal, arXiv:2609.19118v1} assumes a fixed order independent of samples and values and therefore uses a different adversary model.

This work was developed with Codex assistance. The paper's author is Ryan Shea. The written arguments and exact programs have same-agent verification; independent mathematical review and formalization of these refinements remain pending. No exhaustive priority search, confirmed best-known-bound claim, or practical performance claim is made. The repository uses Apache 2.0, with source attribution in \href{https://github.com/shea256/matroid-prophet-inequality/blob/master/NOTICE}{NOTICE}.
